scope: Research-only reduction of own root actions at a normally initialized singles team preview. No production caller, opponent action reduction or continuation state-key merging.
relation: Same selected roster identities and lead; interchange the two bench positions. Map later switch actions by roster identity. RNG states need not match; compare outcome probabilities and observations.

source_audit.result: Preview legality uses distinct picks and summed levels. Start activates the first selected member. Only three-member picks are reduced; one- and two-member cases retain all actions. Team actions can consume different seeded queue-tie draws, so seed-identical trajectories are not the equivalence claim.

Switches exchange the incoming roster member with the active position; legal switch indices are relabeled. Random drag-in samples the eligible bench. With three selected members there are at most two eligible targets, preserving exact probability under interchange.

Beat Up traverses own party and reveals participating allies in order. Reject all own-roster Beat Up, Metronome, Mimic, Mirror Move, Sketch and Transform slots, including unselected members and both current/base moves. Sleep Talk only calls the current own slots. Opponent-owned Beat Up reads the opponent's party, so the guard does not inspect hidden enemy moves. Heal Bell clears living party statuses without per-bench messages; Nightmare's end message can concern the active member in reachable play because switching clears its volatile.

The sole get_all_pokemon caller emits the original roster before selection. Active protocol labels and event slot handling use position zero. Sleep/freeze clauses test membership. Position-valued persistent effect references are set by active sources in reachable play; Leech Seed resolves only the active slot. Arbitrary injected bench-source volatiles are outside this relation.

checks.guard_and_mask: Both perspectives, all roster sizes one through six, 155 total-level restriction, external reverse-only masks, idempotence, all six unsafe moves, non-preview refusal, index preservation, masked actions unvisited and final choice eligible.
checks.kernel_detail: Two preview-step pairs and 16 post-preview pairs: own Splash/Heal Bell/two identity-mapped switches versus Splash/Whirlwind, from both perspectives. Bench poison states exercise Heal Bell. Every chance branch enumerated with logs enabled; normalized full state hash and complete protocol-log distributions agree.
checks.negative_control: Beat Up from swapped selections reveals the same three allies in different orders. This refutes an unconditional equality of observations, not a measured difference in optimal value.
checks.regression: 226 bot library tests, nine blind-agent tests and four new integration tests passed; all bot targets compile.

limitations: Source reasoning plus finite checks is not a machine-checked equivalence proof over every reachable game state. The engine and chance sampler remain trusted. Search policies and rollout ordering can change after reducing actions even where game choices are equivalent. No better choice, full-game improvement, global optimum or superiority to deployed bot has been established.
